$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡{3x}.$ Then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\left(-\operatorname{sin}⁡{3x}\right)\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\left(\text{d}u\right)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡{3x}\,\text{d}x.

| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{3}}\operatorname{tan}⁡{3x}\,\text{d}x &=\frac{5}{3}\cdot -{\int }_{1}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)}\frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  &=\frac{5}{3}\left(-\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|{|}_{1}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)}\right) \\  &=\frac{5}{3}\left(-\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|\right) \\  &=\frac{5}{3}\left(-\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)|\right).\end{aligned}

We use the identities $\operatorname{tan}⁡{5x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}}$ and $\operatorname{sec}⁡{5x}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}}$ and rewrite the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot \int \operatorname{tan}⁡{5x}\operatorname{sec}^{3}⁡{5x}\,\text{d}x &=6\cdot \int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}}\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}})}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  &=6\cdot \int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}^{3}⁡{5x}}\,\text{d}x \\  &=6\cdot \int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}}{\operatorname{cos}^{4}⁡{5x}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡{5x}.$ Then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\left(-\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}\right)\,⟹\,\frac{1}{5}\left(-\text{d}u\right)=\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot \int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{5x}}{\operatorname{cos}^{4}⁡{5x}}\,\text{d}x &=\frac{6}{5}\cdot \int \frac{1}{{u}^{4}}\,(-\text{d}u) \\  &=\frac{6}{5}\cdot -\int \frac{1}{{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u \\  &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\frac{1}{3{u}^{3}}\right)+C \\  &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\frac{1}{3\operatorname{cos}^{3}⁡{5x}}\right)+C \\  &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sec}^{3}⁡{5x}\right)+C\end{aligned}
$$
